Morphs, Depths, and Frontier Neighbors

Visual art bible for expanding Out of Spec beyond Week 1—defining five starter-to-alien tarantula morphs, three subterranean mining tiers, and your six-character colony cast.

The five starter and alien tarantula morphs

Each morph pairs a distinct micro-climate tolerance band with a specialized bio-material output—so collecting rarer tarantulas directly upgrades your satellite links, rover stability, and compliance clearance.

Morph (L to R) Origin & Vibe Climate Guardband Precision Output & Gameplay Role
1. Cobalt Reference Grounded starter morph 23°C ± 2.0 · 75% RH Reliable baseline optical silk; ideal for first-week dish alignment and learning sensor zeroing.
2. Ember-Knee Grounded arid classic 26°C ± 2.5 · 45% RH Forgiving humidity band; sheds heat-resistant filament that shields rovers near Tier 2 magma vents.
3. Verdant Trace Frontier bio-morph 22°C ± 0.8 · 82% RH Tight calibration window; produces bioluminescent trace-silk required for MegaCorp mid-game audits.
4. Quartz-Spinner Deep-canyon alien morph 19°C ± 0.4 · 88% RH Needs Tier 3 geode substrate; spins crystal-core fiber that cuts deep-cavern satellite lag to near zero.
5. Dune-Ochre Solar-flare survivor 31°C ± 3.0 · 30% RH Thrives during heatwaves and ion storms when outdoor rovers go dark, keeping daily income flowing.

Three-tier mining canyon biomes

Mining in Out of Spec isn’t just swinging a pickaxe at tougher rock—it is a signal-and-drift engineering puzzle. Every deeper layer introduces a new physical obstacle to your orbital link, forcing you to place relay chains and tighten your drill tolerances.

Tier 1 · Terracotta Plateau

Open sky with clean satellite line-of-sight except behind surface boulders. Home to starter crops, shallow cyan quartz fissures, and forgiving rover steering drift.

Tier 2 · Basalt Thermal Tunnels

Overhanging rock arches break direct orbital uplinks—requiring relay beacons at tunnel mouths—while glowing orange magma vents rapidly cook unshielded sensors out of spec.

Tier 3 · Bioluminescent Depths

Total orbital blackout without Quartz-Spinner optical relays. Emerald and violet crystal clusters shatter into low-value dust unless your mining drill is calibrated within sub-percent tolerance.

The six quirky colony neighbors

A tight six-character cast gives your colony town unmistakable personality without turning dialogue writing into a multi-year bottleneck. Every character ties directly into one core progression system.

1. Bram — Scrapyard Mechanic

Grease-stained rover tinkerer who despises corporate checklists. Trades canyon ore for reinforced treads, bigger batteries, and questionable aftermarket steering servos.

2. Lin — Botanical Keeper

Runs the glowing greenhouse dome. Buys your frontier crops, trades exotic terrarium mosses, and slowly flips from spider-phobic to obsessed with your optical silk.

3. Vance — Rival Contractor

Smug MegaCorp favorite in an immaculate lab coat who secretly fudges his uncertainty budgets. Your main comedic foil on colony leaderboards and audit days.

4. Kestrel — Orbital Smuggler

Appears by the drop-pod pad during ion storms with unlicensed alien tarantula slings, gray-market calibration weights, and zero interest in ISO stickers.

5. AUD-1T — Compliance Drone

Hovering MegaCorp sphere with a cheery chime and a glowing amber scanner eye. Issues deeply petty fines for expired stickers and unlogged rover tire pressure.

6. Ollie — Radio Astronomer

Lives beside the perimeter dish wearing oversized glowing headphones. Forecasts incoming solar flares and unlocks deep-sky satellite relay blueprints when you tune his gear.

“Hand the morph table to ChatGPT for balancing JSON, and hand the six character bios to Grok to draft their sharpest colony banter.”

Keep these visual sheets pinned next to MagicaVoxel and Godot 4—every time you add a new tier or neighbor after Week 4, the silhouette, palette, and gameplay hook are already locked.
